Offer ₹552.00 Cr · fresh ₹320.00 Cr · OFS ₹232.00 Cr

props.closer: Education, not advice: read the RHP, decide for yourself.

captions: This is the Orient Cables (India) I P O, a mainboard offer,
open from the twenty-fifth to the twenty-ninth of September.
The price band is ₹258 to ₹272.
Every figure here comes from the final red herring prospectus
and exchange notices;
the final price is fixed after bidding,
so valuations are computed at the ₹272 cap.
First, the business.
Orient Cables makes networking cables,
the LAN cables inside offices and data rooms,
plus specialty power cables,
optical-fibre cables and cable harnesses,
including E V charging-gun assemblies.
The RHP's industry report puts it among India's top four
networking-cable makers,
with about 22.9% share in FY26.
It runs two plants in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan,
and a new Bengaluru plant that started in May 2026.
The financial checkpoint.
FY26 revenue was ₹1,171.65 Cr, against ₹824.96 Cr in FY25,
a change of 42.03%.
Profit after tax was ₹53.81 Cr, a margin of 4.59%.
Here is the catch.
Revenue grew 42.03%, but profit barely moved,
from ₹53.32 Cr to ₹53.81 Cr,
so the margin fell from 6.46% to 4.59%.
The June 2026 quarter looked stronger:
₹489.16 Cr of revenue and ₹33.22 Cr of profit,
though a single quarter is not a full year.
The offer size at the cap is ₹552.00 Cr.
₹320.00 Cr is fresh issue that goes into the company,
and ₹232.00 Cr is an offer for sale that goes to selling shareholders.
So 57.97% of the deal is new capital,
and 42.03% is an exit for existing holders.
Where does the money go?
Of the ₹320.00 Cr fresh issue, ₹155.50 Cr repays debt.
₹91.50 Cr goes to machinery and civil works,
and the rest to general corporate purposes.
The ₹232.00 Cr offer for sale goes to the promoter family and its two trusts,
whose average acquisition cost the ad lists as between zero and ₹0.01 a share.
Now, valuation.
At the ₹272 cap,
the price is 51.61x FY26 earnings per share of ₹5.27.
That sits near the top of its listed cable peers:
Finolex at 26.29x, Havells 42.69x, Polycab 46.69x,
KEI 48.99x and R R Kabel 54.85x.
The RHP's 128.11x industry average is pulled up by Sterlite
Technologies at 708.38x,
so the peer range is the fairer yardstick.
Now balance the evidence.
Watch-out:
PAT flat while revenue grew 42.03%.
Strength:
About 22.9% share of India's networking-cable market.
Watch-out:
51.61x P/E, near the top of listed peers.
Strength:
Strong Q1 FY27:
₹33.22 Cr PAT in one quarter.
Watch-out:
42.03% of the offer is promoter OFS.
Strength:
₹155.50 Cr of fresh money cuts debt.
How to apply.
The minimum bid is one lot of 55 shares,
which is ₹14,960 at the cap.
Retail investors can bid up to two lakh rupees,
and allotment is by lottery if retail is oversubscribed.
Check live subscription on the N S E or B S E website,
not social media.
Let's recap.
FY26 revenue ₹1,171.65 Cr, profit ₹53.81 Cr.
The offer is ₹552.00 Cr, of which ₹232.00 Cr is offer for sale.
Valuation is 51.61x earnings at the cap.
The minimum investment is ₹14,960.
